calls.reason: LLaMA (Feb 2023) and Llama 2 (July 2023) show competitors built strong models from standard, published methods and public data. That backs the copyability point and the stated doubt about a moat, even though the imitation study found base-model advantages.

The evidence is mixed. The citation audit and the robotaxi disruption reports back the claim, but California approved driverless fare service and a mammography trial found AI-assisted screening safe. The coding and board-game evidence is thin or dated.
The packet has no evidence items. No matched records of OpenAI's revenue and operating costs were found, and the killer-app and investor-patience parts have no test that can be checked.
Stack Overflow surveys show AI tool use by developers rising each year from 2023 to 2025, which fits the forecast. But 'for a long time' and 'never go back' have no deadline that has passed.

The only evidence is S&P's forecast of about $3.7B in generative-AI revenue for all of 2023. That is in tension with 'probably not billions', but it is a full-year forecast, not realized cumulative revenue through August 2023, and the claim itself is hedged.

Ford's estimate of more than $100B invested in Level 4 autonomy supports the investment figure. On the revenue side there is only one Mobileye quarter, so the gap is plausible but there is no cumulative revenue total to compare against.
